investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict. The scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any agent VM from being provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules and cannot be used as fallback targets. With no preemption victims available on either eligible node, the scheduler cannot place the pod, so the agent VM is never created, no vmIdPresent or remoteState evidence is produced, and the eval contract fails completely. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval harness defect.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads and none have been released. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector (e.g., a label such as kata-containers=true or a specific node pool label is absent on those nodes), reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity exhaustion on those 2 nodes.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have created remote agent VMs that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from being scheduled. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is only reached if the probe completes; if a prior run was interrupted, cleanup may not have executed.

Lower confidence: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec may be overly restrictive, targeting a node pool that is undersized for the current load, making the cluster structurally unable to absorb concurrent remote-agent eval runs even at normal VM utilization.

If the 4 affinity-excluded nodes were found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the pod's affinity rules were shown to be correct, the diagnosis would shift to a node labeling or pool configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeded without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a brief resource spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the pod spec's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity were found to be set to a value larger than the per-node allocatable limit, the root cause would be a misconfigured resource request rather than capacity exhaustion from concurrent workloads.

If no other pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure, the cause would shift to a node-level resource reporting or kubelet registration defect rather than workload-driven exhaustion.

Add an eval that validates the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec against the actual labels present on cluster nodes, alerting when the effective scheduling domain drops below a minimum threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 schedulable nodes with available capacity).
Add a historical trend eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time across eval runs, enabling detection of gradual capacity erosion before full exhaustion occurs.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector), preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity on the two nodes that carry that resource. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~130–150 seconds before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence and a full contract violation. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata runtime, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, and those nodes are full. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict. The scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any agent VM from being provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules and cannot be used as fallback targets. With no preemption victims available on either eligible node, the scheduler cannot place the pod, so the agent VM is never created, no vmIdPresent or remoteState evidence is produced, and the eval contract fails completely. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the production Kubernetes cluster, not an eval harness defect.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=136533, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling block rather than a timeout
possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, meaning all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads and none have been released. No preemption victims exist, so the scheduler cannot free capacity.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector (e.g., a label such as kata-containers=true or a specific node pool label is absent on those nodes), reducing the effective scheduling domain to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity exhaustion on those 2 nodes.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have created remote agent VMs that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from being scheduled. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is only reached if the probe completes; if a prior run was interrupted, cleanup may not have executed.

Lower confidence: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec may be overly restrictive, targeting a node pool that is undersized for the current load, making the cluster structurally unable to absorb concurrent remote-agent eval runs even at normal VM utilization.

If the 4 affinity-excluded nodes were found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the pod's affinity rules were shown to be correct, the diagnosis would shift to a node labeling or pool configuration error rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeded without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a brief resource spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the pod spec's kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request quantity were found to be set to a value larger than the per-node allocatable limit, the root cause would be a misconfigured resource request rather than capacity exhaustion from concurrent workloads.

If no other pods were found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure, the cause would shift to a node-level resource reporting or kubelet registration defect rather than workload-driven exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity-insufficient' status rather than a generic scheduling timeout.

Add an eval that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods (pods in Pending or Running state with kata.peerpods.io/vm requests that are not associated with an active eval run) exist in the cluster, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Add an eval that validates the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec against the actual labels present on cluster nodes, alerting when the effective scheduling domain drops below a minimum threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 schedulable nodes with available capacity).
Add a historical trend eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time across eval runs, enabling detection of gradual capacity erosion before full exhaustion occurs.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector), preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity on the two nodes that carry that resource. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~130–150 seconds before the eval timed out, producing empty evidence and a full contract violation. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata runtime, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two kata-capable nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving none for new eval pods. This is the primary cause supported by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, and those nodes are full. A misconfiguration of the affinity rules (e.g., overly restrictive selector) could also prevent scheduling even if VM slots were available on other nodes.

Cluster under-provisioning for kata peer-pod workloads: the 6-node cluster may not have enough kata-capable nodes to handle concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads sharing the same resource pool.

Eval concurrency collision: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all ran within the same ~5-minute window and each attempted to schedule a pod, potentially competing for the same limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and exhausting them collectively.

If the two kata-capable nodes show kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity of 0 in their node status (i.e., the resource was never provisioned or was removed), the cause would be a node configuration regression rather than slot exhaustion by running workloads.
If sibling checks for local agents (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata peer-pod layer alone.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-node-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. capacity on all nodes and fails with a clear capacity signal before any pod creation is attempted.

Add a pre-scheduling readiness gate to the remote-agent-create eval that verifies at least one schedulable node exists for the remote agent pod spec before proceeding, enabling early WARN rather than a full timeout.
Add a pod-leak detection eval that lists all remote agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found in a non-terminal state, catching slot exhaustion caused by leaked pods.

Add a concurrent-scheduling stress eval that submits two remote agent pods simultaneously and verifies both schedule within the warning latency threshold, surfacing capacity contention before it causes production eval failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required confidential-compute pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was returned by any check, meaning the agent pod never started and the eval runner never reached the stage where it could collect orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the pod cannot be placed on any node in the 6-node cluster. Because the agent pod never becomes Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completes, no evidence is collected, and the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message (check-expectations.json lines 266-270) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' for remote-agent-runtime after 148s unscheduled.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=152200, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-01T18:54:06.293Z — pod timed out before becoming schedulable.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the agent pod never reached a state where the runner could collect any response fields.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduling failure message, pod stuck 131s, latencyMs=136533, evidenceKeys=[] — agent creation also failed.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduling failure message, pod stuck 144s, latencyMs=146631, evidenceKeys=[] — state polling also failed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; this call cannot succeed if the pod is unschedulable.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — assertion is unreachable if the pod never starts.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false, so this failure does not itself trigger a feature outage threshold, but sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (features.json lines 183-184).
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion: all available VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message across all three failing checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch: 4 of 6 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were not exhausted, scheduling might still succeed; the combination of both constraints causes total failure.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes for the current eval workload, especially if multiple concurrent eval runs or production workloads compete for the same resource.

Lower confidence — transient resource contention: a burst of concurrent remote-agent requests (from evals or production) may have temporarily exhausted VM slots that would otherwise be available, making this a timing-sensitive rather than a persistent capacity issue.

reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should fail with the same kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion message if the root cause is cluster-wide.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the Kubernetes cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Query the cluster to see how many kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are allocated vs. available on each of the 2 eligible nodes. Identify which pods are consuming the resource.

reproductionSteps.label: Check node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec
reproductionSteps.details: Review the pod template used by createAgent for 'remote' type to confirm which node labels are required and why only 2 of 6 nodes qualify.

reproductionSteps.label: Observe whether the failure is persistent or transient by re-running the eval after a delay
reproductionSteps.details: If VM slots free up after existing remote-agent pods terminate, the failure may be transient contention rather than a hard capacity ceiling.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports exhaustion of the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes eligible by node affinity, blocking all remote-agent pod creation. Evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create eval check (required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: This required check failed with the same scheduling error (sibling.remote-agent-create). Per features.json line 183, it is required=true, meaning its failure contributes to the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-state eval check (required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: This required check also failed with the same scheduling error (sibling.remote-agent-state). Per features.json line 184, it is required=true and also contributes to the degraded/outage threshold.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check (required=false)
affectedAreas.reason: The primary failing check. Registered as required=false (features.json line 185), so its failure alone does not trigger the outage threshold, but it confirms the scheduling problem is cluster-wide.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: This is the earliest point in the runner where the scheduling failure manifests. The call cannot complete if the pod is unschedulable, preventing all downstream evidence collection.
affectedAreas.details: Line 1918: const agent = await createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId);

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields are missing because the pod never started. The contract violation is a downstream symptom of the scheduling failure.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 eligible nodes. Identify which pods are holding the resource and whether any are stale or leaked from prior eval runs.

Determine whether the remote-agents feature has crossed its degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold (features.json line 187) given that both required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) also failed.

If VM slots are persistently exhausted, evaluate whether additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes can be added to the cluster or whether the node affinity rules can be relaxed to include more of the existing 6 nodes.
Review the pod node affinity and selector configuration for remote-agent pods to confirm that restricting scheduling to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional and not a misconfiguration.

Determine whether concurrent eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, and consider serializing eval runs or adding resource quotas to prevent eval workloads from starving production capacity (or vice versa).

Once the scheduling issue is resolved, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm that evidence is collected and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message, and 'hello from aura' assertion) is satisfied.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is persistent or has resolved. If it recurs with the same message, capacity is the confirmed constraint.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Verifies that all three checks share the same root cause and that no check has recovered independently.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Query kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the VM slot exhaustion hypothesis and identifies which workloads are consuming capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Use kubectl to describe nodes and identify allocatable vs. allocated kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on each node. Identify which pods hold the resource.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect pod node affinity and selector rules for remote-agent pod template
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4-node affinity mismatch is expected configuration or a misconfiguration that is unnecessarily restricting the schedulable pool.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec used by createAgent for the 'remote' type and verify which node labels are required, confirming why only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect implicated source paths for recent changes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Rules out an eval-runner or config change as a contributing factor to the scheduling failure.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Review infra/evals/status/features.json, infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, and infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs for any changes that may have altered pod resource requests or node selectors.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and another cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure, or runner bug) would need to be investigated.
If re-running the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and returned all required evidence fields, the failure would be transient contention rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If the scheduler message were absent from a re-run but the eval still failed with empty evidence, the root cause would shift to the eval runner or API layer (e.g., createAgent returning without a pod, or a network/auth issue).

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would not explain the pattern and a check-specific runner bug would be more likely.
If the node affinity rules were recently changed to exclude more nodes, that configuration change would be a contributing cause; absence of such a change would keep the focus on VM slot exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all eligible nodes, alerting before slots are fully exhausted rather than after a pod fails to schedule.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agents eval suite that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available before attempting agent creation, producing a clearer SKIP or WARN result instead of a timeout-based FAIL.
Add a historical trend eval that tracks remote-agent pod scheduling latency over time, enabling detection of gradual capacity degradation before full exhaustion occurs.
Consider adding a canary eval that runs at lower frequency and lower resource cost to detect node affinity misconfigurations independently of VM slot availability.
